chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa.

He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me one day: Do you know how to pray, O Hammad? He said: So I said: O my master, I have memorized the book of Hariz on prayer. He said: So he said: Never mind, stand and pray. He said: So I stood in front of him facing the qibla, and I commenced the prayer, bowed and prostrated. Then he said: O Hammad, you do not know how to pray! How repulsive it is for a man to have sixty years or seventy years pass over him and yet not establish a single prayer with its complete limits!

Hammad said: So abasement befell me within myself and I said: May I be your sacrifice, teach me the prayer. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) stood facing the qibla, erect, and released both his hands upon his thighs with his fingers joined together, and drew his feet close until there was a gap of three fingers between them spread apart, and he turned the toes of both his feet toward the qibla, neither deflected from it, in submissiveness and tranquility, and said: God is Greatest. Then he recited al-Hamd with measured intonation and (Say: He is God, the One), then paused briefly for the measure of a breath while standing, then said: God is Greatest, while standing.

Then he bowed and filled his palms over his knees spread apart, and pushed his knees back until his back was level — such that if a drop of water or oil were poured on him it would not slide off due to the evenness of his back — and he extended his neck and lowered his gaze. Then he glorified three times with measured intonation and said: Glorified is my Lord, the Magnificent, and His is the praise. Then he stood erect, and when he was firmly established in standing he said: God hears the one who praises Him. Then he recited the takbir while standing and raised his hands to the level of his face. Then he prostrated and placed his palms with fingers joined together between his knees in front of his face, and said: Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, and His is the praise, three times, and he did not rest any part of his body against another. And he prostrated on eight major limbs:

And he prostrated on eight major limbs: the forehead, the two palms, the two centers of the knees, and the tips of the big toes of both feet — these seven are obligatory — and placing the nose on the ground is recommended (sunnah), and it is the pressing down (al-irghAm). Then he raised his head from the prostration, and when he was settled seated, he said: God is Greatest. Then he sat on his left side, having placed the outer surface of his right foot on the inner surface of his left foot, and said: I seek God's forgiveness, my Lord, and I repent unto Him. Then he recited the takbir while seated and performed the second prostration and said what he had said in the first. He did not lean on any part of his body against anything in the bowing nor the prostration — he was winged (arms extended) — and he did not place his forearms on the ground. So he prayed two rak'as in this manner.
Then he said: O Hammad, pray in this manner: do not look around, do not fidget with your hands and fingers, and do not spit to your right, nor to your left, nor in front of you.

key_terms.التَّرْتِيل: Tartil — measured, deliberate recitation with proper pronunciation
key_terms.الرُّكُوع: Ruku' — the bowing position in prayer
key_terms.السُّجُود: Sujud — prostration; placing the forehead on the ground
key_terms.الْإِرْغَام: Al-Irghaam — the pressing of the nose to the ground; recommended (sunnah) in prostration
key_terms.الْخُشُوع: Khushu' — inward reverence and outward tranquility in prayer
key_terms.الْقِبْلَة: The qibla — the direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca, which Muslims face during prayer
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: An Arabic expression of self-sacrifice and deep reverence: 'May I be your sacrifice'

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teach Hammad ibn Isa to pray correctly?
ai.summary: This hadith records the celebrated account of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) personally demonstrating the correct manner of prayer to his companion Hammad ibn Isa, after rebuking him for not knowing how to pray properly despite memorizing a legal text. The Imam proceeded to model each position of the prayer with precise physical details — stance, hand placement, recitations, ruku', and sujud — specifying what is obligatory and what is recommended. This is one of the most detailed and authoritative Shia hadith on the outward form of salat, preserving the exact bodily postures of the Imam as a living exemplar of the prayer.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from Hammad b. `Isa.

He said: Abu `Abdillah (as) said to me one day: Do you know how to pray, O Hammad? He said: I said: O my master! I comply with the book of Hariz about prayer. He said: So he (as) said: Worry not! Stand and pray. He said: So, I stood in front of him, facing the qibla. Then I commenced the prayer and I bowed and I prostrated. So, he (as) said:  O Hammad! You do not know how to pray. How repulsive is it for a man to have had sixty years or seventy years pass him by, and he has not established a single prayer with all its limits?!

Hammad said: So, abasement befell me within and I said: May I be your sacrifice! Please teach me the prayer. So, Abu `Abdillah (as) stood facing the qibla, erect. Then he placed both his hands together on his thighs, his fingers joined together, and he drew his feet near until they were three digits apart. And he turned, with all the toes of his feet, neither of his feet deflected from the qibla, with submissiveness and complete surrender (tranquility), and said: Allah is the Greatest (Allaahu Akbar)! Then he recited Surat al-Hamd and qul huwallahu ahad with intonation (tartil). Then he paused a little for a measure of one breath while he was standing. Then he said: Allah is the Greatest (Allaahu Akbar) – while he was standing.

Then he bowed and spread his palms over the knees and pushed his knees backwards until his back was straight; were a drop of water or fat to be poured on him, it would not slide down due to the straightening of his back and the pushing back of his knees, and he erected his neck and looked down. Then he glorified thrice with intonation and said: Allah listens to the one who praises Him (sami`allahu liman hamidah). Then he recited the takbir while he was standing and raised his hands opposite his face. And he prostrated and placed his hands on the ground prior to his knees and said: Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, and I praise Him (subhana rabbiya 'l-a`laa wa bi hamdih), thrice, and he did not place (i.e. rest) anything (any part) of his body against anything from it. And he prostrated upon eight major [parts]:

the forehead and the palms and the kneecaps and the tips of the big toes of the feet and the nose; then these are seven, plenty (seven are required). And the positioning of the nose over the earth is recommended. And it is [out of] compulsion (i.e. the nose is forced to rub the ground when the forehead is on the ground). Then he raised his head from prostration and when he was seated, he said: Allah is the Greatest (Allahu akbar)! Then he sat on his left side and he placed the outside of his right foot over the inside of his left foot, and said: I seek forgiveness of Allah, my Lord and I turn towards (repent unto) Him (astaghfirullaha rabbi wa atubu ilayh). Then he recited the takbir while he was seated and he prostrated a second time and said what he had said in the first and he did not resort to anything from his body against another from it either in the ruku` or the sujud, and he was winged (i.e., the placement of his hands appeared as if there were wings on either side) and he did not place his arms on the ground. Then he prayed the second unit similarly,
then said: O Hammad! Pray this way. And do not turn, nor play with your hands or your fingers and do not spit from your right nor your left nor in front of you.
